sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Kent County, Michigan?
sections.html:
A city or township bills the tax, and the county treasurer enters the picture only for parcels that went unpaid. Kent's Bureau of Equalization keeps assessments uniform across 21 townships and nine cities, while each local assessor sets the value on your own parcel.

Use that split to pick the right phone call. A wrong value, a missing exemption or a bill that never showed up goes to the local assessor or treasurer. A balance that was returned unpaid, and any foreclosure auction after a court order, belongs to the Kent County Treasurer, whose counter is on the first floor of the Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, Grand Rapids. Hours run Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.

sections.h2: What does Kent County look like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Kent is the biggest Michigan county outside metro Detroit, and Grand Rapids is both its seat and its largest city. Census figures show 675,232 residents as of July 2025 and 256,648 households in the 2020-2024 survey.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $289,900
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.3%
  • Median household income: $82,631
  • Median gross rent: $1,243

With a typical home near $290,000, a late balance grows into real money fast, because the penalties below are percentages of the unpaid bill. City and township parcels share one collection calendar.

sections.h2: When do unpaid Kent County property taxes become delinquent, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
Kent's local treasurers send bills on July 1 and December 1. Whatever is still open after the following March 1 moves to the county treasurer, with a 4% fee and monthly interest of 1% on top. The county FAQ is blunt that no rule allows those charges to be waived, including for an owner whose bill never arrived.

Summer bills have an earlier pinch point. MCL 211.44a puts the interest start for summer tax at September 15. The county's later steps follow a fixed calendar:

Kent County delinquent tax steps and added costs (Kent County Treasurer FAQ; MCL 211.78a)
StageTimingWhat is added
Returned delinquentMarch 1 after the tax year4% fee plus 1% interest per month
ForfeitureMarch 1, one year later$175 title search fee, $60 recording fees, interest rises to 1.5% per month
Foreclosure preparationMarch 31 after the forfeiture dateProperty is readied for a foreclosure judgment

The county sums it up as two years and one month to pay before foreclosure. Its auction list of foreclosed properties appears around July 1 each year.

sections.h2: How can an owner pay delinquent taxes to the Kent County Treasurer?
sections.html:
You can pay online, by phone, by mail, through the Kent County mobile app, or at the counter. Have the parcel number or street address ready for any method.

  • Online: E-check from a bank account has a $0 fee. Credit cards add 2.98%, collected by the card processor and not by the county.
  • Phone: 616-303-7760, option 1 for English or option 2 for Spanish, cards only, with the same processing fee.
  • Mail: Checks or money orders payable to Kent County Treasurer, P.O. Box Y, Grand Rapids, MI 49501-4925, with the parcel ID written on the memo line.
  • In person: The counter is meant for transactions that require cash. Others are encouraged to pay online or by mail.

You may send a partial payment at any time, though the charges keep running against what remains. Kent County does not honor postmarks. The payment has to arrive before the end of a month to count at that month's payoff figure, so call 616-632-7500 for the current payoff before sending a check.

sections.h2: Can a Kent County owner delay foreclosure with a hardship deferral?
sections.html:
Yes, for up to one year, if the owner qualifies and applies in time. To qualify for the Financial Hardship program you must hold title by recorded deed or land contract, occupy the property as your principal residence, and document a substantial hardship.

The application asks for a payment plan on page 3. A plan can include regular payments or a record of them, help from a local assistance agency, or the sale or refinancing of the property. The form must be in before March 1, and the treasurer's office does not promise approval. A deferral is also a one-time tool, and it does not reduce the bill: interest and fees continue to pile up during the extension.

For a homeowner who plans to sell, that last point is the one to weigh. The deferral buys time to close a sale, and the balance still comes out of the sale price.

sections.h2: Where does a Kent County owner take a value complaint?
sections.html:
Start at the assessor's office in your city or township. The Kent County treasurer's own FAQ says it does not handle value complaints, so the county will send you back to the local unit.

Every city and township holds a March board of review under MCL 211.30, and the local assessor can give you the session dates and how to file. A written decision comes by early June, with information on carrying the case to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Boards that meet in July and December look only at qualified errors and a short list of exemption appeals (MCL 211.53b), so a missed March date usually means waiting a year.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs apply in Kent County?
sections.html:
The Principal Residence Exemption and the poverty exemption are the two most owners ask about. The PRE takes the local school operating levy, up to 18 mills, off a home you own and live in. Owners file with the local assessor. The county's stated cutoffs are June 1 for the summer bill and November 1 for the winter bill.

The county FAQ sends a PRE denial from the state to the Michigan Department of Treasury for an informal conference, and a denial from the local unit or county to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Poverty exemption questions go to the city or township assessor. The homestead property tax credit is a separate item, claimed on the Michigan income tax return.

One more tip from the treasurer: escrow does not make you safe. A mortgage servicer can miss a payment after a refinance, and the owner is still the one responsible for checking that the bill was paid.

sections.h2: What happens with property tax when a Kent County house sells?
sections.html:
A Kent County sale can only record cleanly if the tax history is in order. Before a warranty deed records in Kent County, the treasurer certifies the parcel's tax status for a $5 fee (MCL 211.135 requires five years of taxes to be paid). A quitclaim deed that carries no warranty covenants is excepted.

The sale also changes the next bill. The buyer's first full-year bill is figured on the state equalized value instead of your capped taxable value (MCL 211.27a), so expect it to differ from yours. For a seller with a delinquent balance, the closing office requests a payoff from the treasurer and subtracts it from the proceeds.

faqs.q: When does Kent County start charging interest on unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Summer tax collects interest from September 15, and the county adds its own fee on March 1. That date comes from MCL 211.44a. On March 1 the Kent County Treasurer adds a 4% administration fee and 1% interest per month to anything left unpaid, and the county FAQ says none of these charges can be waived.

faqs.q: How long before Kent County can foreclose on a house for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: About two years and one month. Taxes become delinquent March 1, the property is forfeited on the following March 1, and foreclosure preparation begins March 31 after that. After a court order, the treasurer sells parcels that have been delinquent more than 24 months.

faqs.q: Does the hardship deferral lower what I owe Kent County?
faqs.a: No. It moves the foreclosure deadline back by a year at most. Interest and fees continue to accumulate, and the application has to be submitted before March 1 with a plan for paying the taxes.

faqs.q: Who do I call to fight my assessment in Kent County?
faqs.a: Start with your local assessor. The county does not change values, so it sends valuation complaints to the local March board of review, and the Michigan Tax Tribunal hears further appeals.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Kent County back taxes before I sell?
faqs.a: Usually yes, and the payoff is subtracted from your proceeds at closing. A warranty deed needs a certificate that five years of tax are paid. Call 616-632-7500 for a payoff before you pick a closing day.
